A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same dgMARK work. Their text, equations, algorithms, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original watermark detection, perplexity, downstream benchmark, editing-attack and sensitivity results in Sections 4–5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds a diffusion-watermark baseline comparison, automated quality ratings, modulo variants and parallel-decoding results.

M1.justification: The default binary watermark and Algorithms 1–3 remain unchanged. Appendix E.4 adds two procedural extensions: matching among m hash groups, tested with m = 3 and 4, and parallel commitment of matching candidates above confidence 0.9 with a single-token fallback. These are bounded extensions of the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions use C4, Writing Prompts, MMLU, GSM8K and HumanEval, with the same editing and paraphrasing scenarios. The added judge, modulo variants and parallel decoder change assessment or generation procedures within retained coverage.

E2.justification: v2 newly evaluates Gloaguen et al.'s diffusion-language-model watermark in Table 12 on detection and downstream benchmarks. v1 only cited this work. Existing KGW and PATTERN-MARK comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce GPT-4o-mini ratings of coherence, clarity and naturalness on a 1–5 scale, modulo settings m = 3 and 4, and parallel decoding with a 0.9 confidence threshold. The added comparator uses multinomial sampling at temperature 0.5 and strengths δ = 1 and 2. Previously reported experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 13–15 add a quality check across beam sizes, a modulo-strength ablation and an analysis of quality and detectability under parallel decoding. Existing token-edit, paraphrasing, window-size and generation-length analyses are retained. The new security discussion contains no additional attack experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests for the experimental comparisons. Existing distribution plots and detection statistics are retained; the added tables do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 12–15 substantially extend the reported evidence with diffusion-baseline scores, linguistic-quality ratings, modulo-strength results and parallel-decoding outcomes. For example, Table 14 reports TPR 0.782 for mod 3 and 0.945 for mod 4 under greedy LLaDA 1.5; these are new configurations, not gains for the unchanged default. Tables 9 and 11 also correct five FNR entries, including 0.127 to 0.013 and 0.257 to 0.267. Main-text results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix E.4 generalizes the matching definition from binary parity to m disjoint hash groups indexed by position modulo m. This is a limited mathematical extension. The original factorization, lookahead equations and detection statistics remain, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: watermarking through decoding order without explicit probability modification, strong detectability, limited quality degradation and post-editing robustness. The conclusion's added 'directly' and 'conditional' wording clarifies the already stated distinction rather than changing the main contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 explicitly distinguishes unchanged conditional predictors from changes to the final output distribution through proposal selection. Appendix E adds interpretations of modulo-strength and parallel-decoding tradeoffs, plus discussion of mapping-inference attacks and possible hash rotation. Appendix F explicitly states the empirical dependence on imperfect models, building on v1's existing discussion of ideal order invariance.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-website link, identifies the GPT-4o-mini judge and supplies its complete evaluation prompt. It also documents the new comparator's temperature and the parallel decoder's threshold and fallback. Existing resource, hardware and implementation disclosures in Appendices B–D remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to MirrorMark, Watermark Stealing in Large Language Models and Fast-dLLM for the new judging and parallel-decoding material. It also develops an empirical comparison with the already cited Gloaguen work. The main related-work positioning remains; venue and year updates do not represent additional works.

P1.justification: Changes are localized: a new distributional explanation, expanded Appendix E, a limitations section, acknowledgements and small terminology edits. The main narrative, section sequence and most existing prose are retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 12–15 and a boxed judge prompt. Existing Figures 8 and 9 exchange order, Figures 5–7 gain explanatory axis captions, and qualitative Tables 12–14 become Tables 16–18. Existing plots are retained, with localized relocation and page reflow rather than a visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The diffusion-specific comparator, automated quality check and strength/parallel-decoding analyses address useful gaps in v1's empirical support. The explicit distributional clarification and corrected FNR entries improve precision. These are incremental gains: the central findings remain unchanged, the judge provides only a proxy without uncertainty estimates, and the security suggestions remain untested.
